The REST module lives in a separate repository, `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, not in `openmrs-core`. The core `VisitService.saveVisit` is declared at `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/VisitService.java:222`. Two generic REST resources call it directly:

1. **`VisitResource1_9.save(Visit)`** (lines 251–254) is the main path. It is the `/ws/rest/v1/visit` create and update path via `DelegatingCrudResource`.
2. **`VisitAttributeResource1_9.save(VisitAttribute)`** (lines 96–116) calls `saveVisit` at line 114 and backs `/ws/rest/v1/visitattribute`.
3. **`VisitAttributeResource1_9.delete`** (lines 122–127) calls `saveVisit` at line 126 to soft-delete an attribute.

The REST module's tests also call `saveVisit` directly. They are not production code, but they would break if the behaviour changed. These are `VisitController1_9Test.java:277` and `EncounterController1_9Test.java:359`.

Core-side callers, for context: `PatientServiceImpl` (line 649), `EncounterServiceImpl` (line 257), and `VisitServiceImpl` itself. The REST module reaches those only indirectly, through encounter or patient saves.
